domain_narrative: A municipal aquatic center project requires the design and installation of a closed-loop pool water treatment and recirculation system serving three pools: a 50-meter competition pool, a leisure pool, and a children's splash pool. The requirements govern turnover rates, chemical dosing, filtration media, and flow balancing to ensure water quality and patron safety across all three pools simultaneously. All requirements were developed jointly by the mechanical engineer of record and the local public health authority and are intended to be read together.

provenance.mutation_authored_by: claude-sonnet-5 (assistant) hand-revision under direct human review, CLAUDE-P22
provenance.revision_reason: The original candidate's mutation ("shall be rated for continuous service ... up to 3.0 ppm") was REJECTED by the CLAUDE-P21 admission gate: in real specification-writing convention, a "shall be rated for up to X" REQUIREMENT clause is standardly read as a MINIMUM required capability, not a maximum ceiling, so a component rated to the reference clause's 5.0 ppm trivially also satisfied the mutated clause's 3.0 ppm floor - no genuine conflict. This revision rewrites the mutation using unmistakable ceiling/prohibition language (an explicit exposure prohibition plus an explicit isolate/bypass mandate during a named, required operational event), and adds a false-positive control (SPEC-22-41-07) using genuine minimum-capability language, so the investigator must distinguish minimum equipment rating, maximum allowed exposure, and required operating condition from each other.

requirements.text: The recirculation system shall achieve a complete water turnover for the 50-meter competition pool within a maximum of 6 hours, for the leisure pool within a maximum of 4 hours, and for the children's splash pool within a maximum of 2 hours, with all three pools operating simultaneously at design flow rates.

Each pool shall be served by a dedicated variable-speed recirculation pump sized to deliver no less than 110% of the flow rate required to achieve the turnover periods stated in SPEC-22-41-01, thereby providing a minimum 10% hydraulic reserve under simultaneous full-operation conditions.

Filtration for each pool shall be provided by pressure sand filters loaded with NSF/ANSI 50-certified filter media. Filter vessel sizing shall be selected so that the design flow rate through the media does not exceed 15 gallons per minute per square foot of filter bed area for any pool under the conditions defined in SPEC-22-41-01.

Automated chemical dosing equipment shall maintain free chlorine residual between 1.0 ppm and 3.0 ppm and pH between 7.2 and 7.6 in each pool at all times during occupied hours. Dosing system sensors shall be installed on the return line of each pool's recirculation loop, downstream of the filtration vessels described in SPEC-22-41-03 and upstream of the pool inlets.

A common surge tank with a minimum working volume equal to 10% of the combined water volume of all three pools shall be provided. The surge tank shall be hydraulically connected to the return side of each pool's recirculation loop and shall serve as the suction source for the recirculation pumps specified in SPEC-22-41-02, ensuring pump suction is never drawn directly from pool floor or wall fittings.

All pipe, fittings, valves, and pump casings in contact with pool water, including dosing system components installed in the recirculation loop, shall be fabricated from or lined with materials rated for continuous service in chlorinated water at free chlorine concentrations up to 5.0 ppm and pH values within the range of 7.0 to 8.0. Separately, the Facility's shock chlorination protocol, mandated by the local public health authority, is performed during non-occupied hours and requires the entire recirculation and dosing system - with no component isolated, bypassed, or shut down for any reason - to remain in continuous operation while free chlorine is elevated to 5.0 ppm during each shock chlorination treatment.

The dosing system's control panel enclosure, which is NOT a wetted component and is not in contact with pool water or dosing chemicals, shall be rated for a minimum IP54 ingress protection level and shall be located in a ventilated, chlorine-off-gas-resistant area; the enclosure is not subject to the wetted-component material rating requirements of SPEC-22-41-06.

proposed_mutation.mutated_text: Automated chemical dosing equipment shall maintain free chlorine residual between 1.0 ppm and 3.0 ppm and pH between 7.2 and 7.6 in each pool at all times during occupied hours. Dosing system sensors shall be installed on the return line of each pool's recirculation loop, downstream of the filtration vessels described in SPEC-22-41-03 and upstream of the pool inlets. Wetted components of the dosing system shall not be exposed to free chlorine concentrations exceeding 3.0 ppm under any operating condition, and the dosing system shall be automatically isolated or bypassed during any shock chlorination treatment conducted under SPEC-22-41-06.
proposed_mutation.description: SPEC-22-41-04 (as revised) prohibits exposing dosing system wetted components to free chlorine above 3.0 ppm and mandates that the dosing system be automatically isolated or bypassed during any shock chlorination event - explicitly naming SPEC-22-41-06's own shock chlorination treatment. But SPEC-22-41-06 explicitly requires all wetted components, INCLUDING dosing system components installed in the recirculation loop, to remain in continuous service THROUGHOUT each shock chlorination treatment (up to 5.0 ppm) without interruption to filtration or recirculation. The two requirements are directly, operationally incompatible during every shock chlorination event: SPEC-22-41-04 mandates isolating/bypassing the dosing system, while SPEC-22-41-06 mandates it remain in continuous, uninterrupted service - for the exact same real, required, recurring operational event, not a hypothetical or unreached one.

proposed_answer_key.expected_detection: A correct reviewer should flag that SPEC-22-41-04 (revised) requires the dosing system to be isolated or bypassed during any shock chlorination event exceeding 3.0 ppm, while SPEC-22-41-06 requires all wetted components - explicitly including dosing system components - to remain in continuous, uninterrupted service throughout every such event (which the public health authority mandates and which reaches up to 5.0 ppm). These two requirements cannot both be satisfied during any actual shock chlorination treatment.
non_defects: SPEC-22-41-01: Defines turnover periods only; no chemical or material content. No conflict introduced.
SPEC-22-41-02: Addresses pump sizing as a percentage of design flow rate; no chemical or material content. No conflict introduced.
SPEC-22-41-03: Addresses filter media type and bed loading rate; no chemical or material content. No conflict introduced.
SPEC-22-41-05: Addresses surge tank volume and hydraulic connection; no chemical or material content. No conflict introduced.

SPEC-22-41-07: A minimum-capability (floor) requirement ("minimum IP54") for a component EXPLICITLY stated to be non-wetted and explicitly exempt from SPEC-22-41-06's scope. This is a false-positive/scope control: a shallow chlorine-keyword or equipment-category match might flag it, but a correct reviewer must recognize the explicit exemption and NOT flag it against SPEC-22-41-06 or the SPEC-22-41-04 mutation.
